arxiv-2012-04815.title: From multi-gravitons to Black holes: The role of complex saddles
arxiv-2012-04815.creator: Alejandro Cabo-Bizet
arxiv-2012-04815.description: Abstract By applying the Atiyah-Bott-Berline-Vergne equivariant integration formula upon double dimensional integrals, we find a way to compute the matrix integral representations of 4 ​ d 4d 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 superconformal indices. The final formula allows us to easily extract analytic results in the large-rank expansion of certain theories.

arxiv-2012-10270.title: On the controversial turbulent Schmidt number value in particle-laden boundary layer flows
arxiv-2012-10270.creator: J. Chauchat, D. Hurther, T. Revil-Baudard, Z. Cheng, T.-J. Hsu
arxiv-2012-10270.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by J. Chauchat, D. Hurther, T. Revil-Baudard, Z. Cheng, T.-J. Hsu. One of the most enigmatic science question concerning inertial particle transport by a turbulent boundary layer flow is the value of the turbulent Schmidt number defined as the ratio of turbulent eddy viscosity to particle concentration diffusivity. Using direct acoustic measurement of turbulent particle flux profile, and two-phase flow turbulence-resolving numerical simulation, it is demonstrated that turbulent dispersion of particles is reduced rather than enhanced as predicted by many existing literature models.

arxiv-2106-16094.title: Analysis of COVID-19 evolution based on testing closeness of sequential data
arxiv-2106-16094.creator: Tomoko Matsui, Nourddine Azzaoui, Daisuke Murakami
arxiv-2106-16094.description: Abstract A practical algorithm has been developed for closeness analysis of sequential data that combines closeness testing with algorithms based on the Markov chain tester. It was applied to reported sequential data for COVID-19 to analyze the evolution of COVID-19 during a certain time period (week, month, etc.).

arxiv-2204-13849.title: Goldilocks-curriculum Domain Randomization and Fractal Perlin Noise with Application to Sim2Real Pneumonia Lesion Detection
arxiv-2204-13849.creator: Takahiro Suzuki, Shouhei Hanaoka, Issei Sato
arxiv-2204-13849.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Takahiro Suzuki, Shouhei Hanaoka, Issei Sato. A computer-aided detection (CAD) system based on machine learning is expected to assist radiologists in making a diagnosis. It is desirable to build CAD systems for the various types of diseases accumulating daily in a hospital. An obstacle in developing a CAD system for a disease is that the number of medical images is typically too small to improve the performance of the machine learning model.

arxiv-2405-07487.title: An Efficient Compression Method for Sign Information of DCT Coefficients via Sign Retrieval
arxiv-2405-07487.creator: Chihiro Tsutake, Keita Takahashi, Toshiaki Fujii
arxiv-2405-07487.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Chihiro Tsutake, Keita Takahashi, Toshiaki Fujii. Compression of the sign information of discrete cosine transform coefficients is an intractable problem in image compression schemes due to the equiprobable occurrence of the sign bits. To overcome this difficulty, we propose an efficient compression method for such sign information based on phase retrieval, which is a classical signal restoration problem attempting to find the phase information of discrete Fourier transform coefficients from their magnitudes.

arxiv-2407-21324.title: Towards Variable-Length In-Network Caching
arxiv-2407-21324.creator: Gyuyeong Kim
arxiv-2407-21324.description: Abstract We present StarCache, a new in-network caching architecture that can cache variable-length items to balance a wide range of key-value workloads. Unlike existing works, StarCache does not cache hot items in the switch memory. Instead, we make hot items revisit the switch data plane continuously by exploiting packet recirculation.

arxiv-2508-10902.title: Web-Halo Model (WHM): Accurate non-linear matter power spectrum predictions without free parameters 2025 Web-Halo Model (WHM): Accurate non-linear matter power spectrum predictions without free parameters – 12
arxiv-2508-10902.creator: S. Brieden, F. Beutler, M. Pellejero-Ibañez
arxiv-2508-10902.description: Abstract We present a parameter-free variant of the halo model that significantly improves the precision of matter clustering predictions, particularly in the challenging 1-halo to 2-halo transition regime, where standard halo models often fail. Unlike HMcode-2020 , which relies on 12 phenomenological parameters, our approach achieves comparable or superior accuracy without any free fitting parameters.

arxiv-2511-10782.title: Historical Surveys to Rubin First Look: Absolute Colors of trans-Neptunian objects astropy ( 8 ; 7 ) ; pandas ( 40 ; 46 )
arxiv-2511-10782.creator: Milagros Colazo, Alvaro Alvarez-Candal
arxiv-2511-10782.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Milagros Colazo, Alvaro Alvarez-Candal. We present a comprehensive photometric study of trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) by combining data from SDSS, Col-OSSOS, DES, and the recent Rubin First Look (RFL) data. Our database comprises 43 878 measurements in the u u , g g , r r , i i , z z , and J J filters, from which we derived 8 738 phase curves for 1 921 unique objects.

pmc-10575211.title: The Effect of Using a Rehabilitation Robot for Patients with Post-Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) Fatigue Syndrome
pmc-10575211.creator: Tomasz Trzmiel, Renata Marchewka, Anna Pieczyńska, Ewa Zasadzka, Igor Zubrycki, Dominika Kozak, Michał Mikulski, Anna Poświata, Sławomir Tobis, Katarzyna Hojan, Iulian I Iordachita
pmc-10575211.description: The aim of this study was to compare the effectiveness of traditional neurological rehabilitation and neurological rehabilitation combined with a rehabilitation robot for patients with post-COVID-19 fatigue syndrome. Eighty-six participants transferred from intensive care units due to post-viral fatigue after COVID-19 were randomly divided into two groups: the intervention group and the control group.

pmc-11478243.title: Oxidative Catalytic Depolymerization of Lignin into Value-Added Monophenols by Carbon Nanotube-Supported Cu-Based Catalysts
pmc-11478243.creator: Chen Tang, Yang Cao, Jie Gao, Gang Luo, Jiajun Fan, James H Clark, Shicheng Zhang, Albin Pintar
pmc-11478243.description: Lignin valorisation into chemicals and fuels is of great importance in addressing energy challenges and advancing biorefining in a sustainable manner. In this study, on the basis of the high microwave absorption performance of carbon nanotubes (CNTs), a series of copper-oxide-loaded CNT catalysts (CuO/CNT) were developed to facilitate the oxidative depolymerization of lignin under microwave heating.

pmc-11510321.title: Detoxification of Acrylamide by Potentially Probiotic Strains of Lactic Acid Bacteria and Yeast
pmc-11510321.creator: Agnieszka Maher, Karolina Miśkiewicz, Justyna Rosicka-Kaczmarek, Adriana Nowak, Urszula Kotowska
pmc-11510321.description: Some potentially probiotic strains of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and yeast that inhabit the digestive tract of humans are known to detoxify xenobiotics, including acrylamide (AA). The objective of the subsequent research was to evaluate the AA-detoxification capability of LAB and yeast isolated from various sources.

pmc-13059510.title: Predictive role of surgical Apgar score for postoperative complications and survival in patients receiving esophagectomy: a meta-analysis
pmc-13059510.creator: Tie Yang, Wei Zheng, Tianli Zuo, Chao Cheng
pmc-13059510.description: PurposeThe association between surgical Apgar score (SAS) and clinical outcomes among patients undergoing esophagectomy remains uncertain now. This study aimed to further identify the predictive role of SAS for postoperative complications and survival in patients receiving esophagectomy.MethodPubMed, EMbase and Web of Science databases were searched up to March 27, 2025.

pmc-13163192.title: The oral vaccine intrOv is attenuated in infecting the lower airway and inducing chronic pathology
pmc-13163192.creator: Zhaoyang Liu, Caiting Li, Sydney Mahan, Jie Ren, Shuping Hou, Guangming Zhong
pmc-13163192.description: The Chlamydia muridarum mutant intrOv is an intracellular oral vaccine vector, as oral inoculation with it induces protection in extra-gut mucosal tissues. Although intrOv is attenuated in both genital and gastrointestinal mucosal tissues, it remains unclear whether intrOv induces pathology in the airway, as wild-type C. muridarum causes severe lung pathology and body weight loss.

pmc-13213301.title: The glenoid track in question: biomechanical considerations for combined inferior glenohumeral ligament repair with glenoid bone loss
pmc-13213301.creator: Dr Parth Aphale, Himanshu Shekhar, Shashank Dokania
pmc-13213301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). nce suggesting that a complementary repair of the posterior band (PB) of the inferior glenohumeral ligament (IGHL) significantly enhances glenohumeral stability compared to isolated anterior repair, even in the presence of a 20% anterior glenoid bone defect (GBD). This finding challenges the traditional focus of Bankart repair and highlights the critical role of the PB in resisting anteroinferior displacement, particularly under higher loads (30 N and 40 N).

Recent genomic studies have identified several virulence-associated genes (VAGs), including SSU_RS09155, SSU_RS09525, and SSU_RS03100, as potential markers of pathogenicity. The current study evaluated the direct contribution of these genes to S.

pmc-13234254.title: Handling persistent cardiac troponin elevation in asymptomatic athletes: The role of macrocomplexes
pmc-13234254.creator: Simon Wernhart, Martin Halle, Sebastian Zenk
pmc-13234254.description: Study objectiveReturn-to-play (RTP) decision includes cardiac troponin I returning to baseline. Formation of antibodies to cardiac troponin I (macrocomplexes) may lead to persistent, false positively elevated cardiac troponin I and may induce unnecessary exclusion from competitive sports.DesignSingle-centre retrospective study.SettingSports cardiological outpatient clinic.

pmc-13333050.title: Paid homecare worker support for people living with motor neurone disease: A secondary analysis of people living with motor neurone disease and family member perspectives
pmc-13333050.creator: Eleanor Wilson, Nicola Turner, Geraldine Macdonald, Christina Faull
pmc-13333050.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:People living with motor neurone disease (MND) increasingly receive complex, life-sustaining interventions at home, including ventilation, tube feeding, and cough assist support. These demands place substantial strain on family carers and often require input from paid homecare workers.

pmc-13586672.title: Comparative Evaluation of Mechanical Properties, Color Stability, and Surface Roughness of Gingiva‐Shaded Composites
pmc-13586672.creator: Faris A Alshahrani, Ibrahim Alsaif, Hassan Alhamza, Abdullah Alhashim, Saleh Alrashed, Noha Taymour, Mohammed M Gad, Hamad Alrumaih, Yousif A Al-Dulaijan, Abdulrahman A Balhaddad, Hannah Wesley
pmc-13586672.description: ObjectiveThis study evaluated the mechanical properties, surface topography, and color stability of a conventional acrylic resin compared to three commercially available gingiva‐shaded composites after immersion in common beverages.MethodologyConventional acrylic resin (Major Base 20) was compared with three commercially available pink composites: Shofu Beautifil II (Shofu Inc.), Beauty Gum Gingiva (TuskDent), and Dengen Dent (Dengen Dent).

pmc-13637127.title: Dynamic changes in the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (ΔAISI) predict postoperative complications following ileostomy closure in rectal cancer patients
pmc-13637127.creator: Mesut Yavaş, Selim Keçeoğlu, Ramazan Kozan, Mehmet Akif Türkoğlu, Mustafa Şare
pmc-13637127.description: BackgroundIleostomy closure following rectal cancer surgery is generally considered a low-risk procedure; however, postoperative complications remain clinically relevant. Reliable and easily accessible biomarkers for predicting these complications are lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of dynamic changes in the aggregate index of systemic inflammation (ΔAISI) for postoperative complications following ileostomy closure.
